mainTopic: Witnesses disqualified for gambling, taking interest and selling טריפה meat, and how such a person can become valid again.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge to רמי בר חמא about whether the חכמים argue with רבי יהודה over a dice player (משחק בקוביא). The גמרא answers that different אמוראים simply hold different views. A ברייתא that disqualifies every dice player is then shown to follow רבי טרפון, who holds that an uncertain commitment does not take effect. Next, רבא rules that a borrower with interest is also disqualified, and the גמרא reads the משנה as 'a loan with interest' to include him. In the story of בר ביניתוס, רבא accepts the borrower's testimony against the lender, because a person cannot make himself a רשע. A butcher who sold טריפה meat cannot be trusted again just by looking sorry. He must give up something valuable in a place where no one knows him. Finally, the גמרא explains מפריחי יונים in two ways, betting on pigeon races or luring pigeons from other people's property (ארא). It then begins to show why the משנה needs both the dice case and the pigeon case, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: When and In What Case only explain
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of the rule of רבי יהושע בן לוי. When רבי יהודה opens with 'אימתי' or 'במה', he is only explaining the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי יהודה says 'When?' or 'In what case?', he is only coming to explain what the חכמים said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the rule of רבי יהושע בן לוי, which it began on the previous page. That rule is the problem for רמי בר חמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, רבי יהודה says 'אימתי', meaning 'when does this apply?' By this rule he is only explaining the חכמים, so everyone agrees that a dice player with another job is kosher. That clashes with רמי בר חמא, who disqualifies him even then.

keyTerms.meaning: When? A word that opens a limiting explanation
In what case? Another word that opens a limiting statement
To explain

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It is the end of a quote from רבי יהושע בן לוי that began on the previous page.

phrases.english: 'When' and 'In what case'
is only to explain the words of the Sages.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: When רבי יהודה says 'אימתי' or 'במה', he is explaining the חכמים, not arguing with them.

steps.title: Even רבי יוחנן agrees that 'When' only explains
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן argues about 'במה', which he says means a disagreement. But he agrees that 'אימתי' is only an explanation. So everyone agrees, and רמי בר חמא is left without support.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: 'When' is to explain, and 'In what case' is to disagree. So according to everyone, 'When' is to explain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי יוחנן, who disagrees with רבי יהושע בן לוי only about 'במה'. It points out that both agree 'אימתי' is an explanation, which makes the problem for רמי בר חמא stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה uses the word 'אימתי'. Both אמוראים agree that this word means רבי יהודה is not arguing. So no one seems to allow a view that disqualifies a dice player who has another job, and that is exactly what רמי בר חמא holds.

keyTerms.meaning: To disagree
According to everyone

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
'When' is to explain,
and 'In what case' is to disagree.
So according to everyone, 'When' is to explain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second אמורא who agrees about 'אימתי', making the challenge stronger.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא, who says a dice player is disqualified even if he has another job
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Everyone agrees 'אימתי' means רבי יהודה is only explaining. So the חכמים also say that a dice player with another job is kosher, which goes against רמי בר חמא.

steps.title: Different אמוראים, different views
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that you cannot challenge one אמורא with another. רמי בר חמא simply holds that the חכמים and רבי יהודה do argue.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are you setting one man against another man? One master holds they disagree, and one master holds they do not disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רמי בר חמא. He does not have to accept the rule of רבי יהושע בן לוי or רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר חמא holds that רבי יהודה argues with the חכמים even when he says 'אימתי'. רבי יהושע בן לוי and רבי יוחנן hold there is no argument. This is a real disagreement between אמוראים, not a mistake by רמי בר חמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Are you setting one man against another? Meaning you cannot attack one אמורא with another's opinion
One master holds
They disagree

phrases.english: Are you setting one man against another man?
One master holds: they disagree,
phrases.notes: This is רמי בר חמא: the חכמים and רבי יהודה really argue.

phrases.english: and one master holds: they do not disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Disagreement between אמוראים: one אמורא's view is no challenge to another's
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone holds that 'אימתי' means no argument, so רמי בר חמא has no support.
steps.terutzMaskana: רמי בר חמא holds that רבי יהודה and the חכמים do argue, so he does not accept that rule.
steps.whatToRemember: An answer like 'גברא אגברא קא רמית' means one אמורא is free to disagree with another. You cannot use one to disprove the other.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows they do argue
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the view that there is no argument. It quotes a ברייתא that disqualifies a dice player whether or not he has another job.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do they not disagree? But it was taught: whether he has a job other than this one, or he has no job except this one, he is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the view of רבי יהושע בן לוי and רבי יוחנן with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא disqualifies even a dice player who has another job. That goes against רבי יהודה, so it seems some view does argue with him, which supports רמי בר חמא. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: A job or trade
Disqualified, here from being a witness

phrases.english: And do they not disagree? But it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אוּמָּנוּת שֶׁלֹּא הוּא,
phrases.english: whether he has a job other than this one,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אוּמָּנוּת אֶלָּא הוּא –
phrases.english: or whether he has no job except this one,
he is disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the view mentioned in step 3 that there is no argument, and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רבי יהושע בן לוי and רבי יוחנן that the חכמים do not argue with רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא disqualifies a dice player even when he has another job. So some תנא really does argue with רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The dice-player ברייתא follows רבי טרפון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא disqualifying every dice player is not the view of the חכמים. It follows רבי יהודה quoting רבי טרפון, who holds that a commitment made without certainty does not take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: That ברייתא follows רבי יהודה in the name of רבי טרפון. As it is taught: רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי טרפון, neither of them ever becomes a נזיר, because נזירות only takes effect when it is stated clearly and with certainty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the view that the חכמים and רבי יהודה do not argue. It says the ברייתא from step 4 belongs to a different תנא, רבי טרפון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון holds that an uncertain promise does not take effect, as we see from his ruling about נזירות. A dice player only promises to pay because he expects to win, so the money he wins is never truly given to him. That is why this ברייתא disqualifies him even if he has another job. The חכמים of our משנה may disagree, so the ברייתא is no challenge to them.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who takes a vow to avoid wine, haircuts, and contact with the dead
The status of being a נזיר
A clear, definite statement made with certainty

steps.confusionAlert: The נזיר case seems unrelated to dice. רבי טרפון's ruling about נזירות is quoted only to show his general rule that an uncertain commitment does not count, and that same rule explains his view about the dice player.

phrases.aramaic: הָהִיא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן הִיא,
phrases.english: That [ברייתא] is Rabbi Yehuda in the name of Rabbi Tarfon,
phrases.notes: "That" means the ברייתא about the dice player quoted in the previous step.

phrases.english: as it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Tarfon:
actually, neither one of them is a nazir,
phrases.notes: The case is two people arguing, where each vows to become a נזיר if the other one turns out to be right.

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא נִתְּנָה נְזִירוּת אֶלָּא לְהַפְלָאָה.
phrases.english: because nezirut was only given for a clear, definite statement.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to show that the חכמים disqualify every dice player, which would mean they disagree with רבי יהודה
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי טרפון's rule that an uncertain commitment does not take effect, so it says nothing about the חכמים

steps.title: רבא: the borrower with interest is also disqualified
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה, one who lends with interest. רבא rules that the borrower who pays interest is also disqualified from testifying.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one who lends with interest. רבא said: one who borrows with interest is disqualified from testimony.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the משנה's next case, and רבא adds that the borrower is disqualified too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions only the lender. רבא extends the disqualification to the borrower, because the borrower also takes part in the forbidden loan.

keyTerms.meaning: One who lends money with interest
One who borrows money with interest
Disqualified from serving as a witness

phrases.english: One who lends with interest.
Rava said: One who borrows with interest
is disqualified from testimony.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on the next case in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A borrower who pays interest is disqualified from testimony

steps.title: The משנה mentions only the lender
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא, because the משנה says "one who lends," which seems to mean only the lender is disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in the משנה: one who lends with interest?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבא's ruling from the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה names only the lender. That suggests the borrower is not disqualified, which goes against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in the משנה)?

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:
"one who lends with interest"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling from step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the borrower is disqualified
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה names only the lender, which implies the borrower is not disqualified

steps.title: Read the משנה as "a loan with interest"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה's word should be read as "a loan that comes with interest," which includes everyone involved in the loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means: a loan that comes with interest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rereads the משנה's word so that it fits רבא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same letters מלוה can be read as מַלְוֶה, "a lender," or as מִלְוָה, "a loan." Read as "a loan," the משנה disqualifies everyone involved in an interest loan, and that includes the borrower.

keyTerms.meaning: A loan
That comes with interest

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's rule stands: both the lender and the borrower in an interest loan are disqualified as witnesses.

phrases.english: A loan that comes with interest.
phrases.notes: Same letters as the משנה's word, read with different vowels: "a loan" instead of "a lender."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to disqualify only the lender
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks of the whole loan, so everyone in it is disqualified, including the borrower

steps.title: רבא disqualifies בר ביניתוס
steps.stepSummary: Two witnesses testified that בר ביניתוס lent with interest. One saw it happen, and the other was the borrower himself. רבא disqualified בר ביניתוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two witnesses testified about בר ביניתוס. One said: he lent with interest in front of me. The other said: he lent me money with interest. רבא disqualified בר ביניתוס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about how רבא ruled in a real case. This story sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two witnesses are needed to disqualify someone. Here, one of the two witnesses was the very person who borrowed from בר ביניתוס with interest, and רבא still accepted the testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: They testified
Witnesses
He lent with interest
He disqualified him

phrases.aramaic: בַּר בִּינִיתּוֹס אַסְהִידוּ בֵּיהּ תְּרֵי סָהֲדֵי.
phrases.english: Regarding bar Binittos, two witnesses testified about him.

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: קַמֵּי דִּידִי אוֹזֵיף בְּרִיבִּיתָא,
phrases.english: One said: In front of me he lent with interest,
and one said: He lent me with interest.
Rava disqualified bar Binittos.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּר בִּינִיתּוֹס אַסְהִידוּ בֵּיהּ תְּרֵי סָהֲדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells a case ruled by the same רבא whose rule appears in step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא disqualified בר ביניתוס based on two witnesses, one of whom was his own borrower

steps.title: How could רבא accept the borrower as a witness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: רבא himself rules that a borrower with interest is a רשע and disqualified. So the second witness, who admitted borrowing with interest, should not be accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't רבא the one who said that one who borrows with interest is disqualified from testimony? So that witness is a רשע, and the תורה says: "Do not place a רשע as a witness."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction between רבא's rule and his ruling in the story. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By his own words, the second witness borrowed with interest, so by רבא's rule he is a רשע. A רשע cannot testify, which leaves only one valid witness. So it seems בר ביניתוס should not have been disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: A wicked person, who is disqualified from testifying
"Do not place a wicked person as a witness"
But isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But isn't Rava the one who said:
one who borrows with interest is disqualified from testimony,
and so he is a wicked person,
phrases.notes: "He" is the second witness, who said he himself borrowed from בר ביניתוס.

phrases.english: and the Torah said: "Do not place a wicked person as a witness."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling in step 9 using his own rule from step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's acceptance of the borrower's testimony against בר ביניתוס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By רבא's own rule the borrower is a רשע and cannot testify, so only one valid witness remains

steps.title: A person cannot make himself wicked
steps.stepSummary: רבא accepted the borrower's testimony because a person cannot make himself a רשע. His words count against בר ביניתוס but not against himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא follows his own reasoning, because רבא said: A person is his own relative, and a person cannot make himself wicked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 10. רבא has a rule that a person's testimony about his own sin does not count against himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was: if the borrower admits to paying interest, he is a רשע and should be disqualified. The answer is that a person is like a relative to himself, and relatives cannot testify. So the part of his testimony about himself is ignored, and only the part about בר ביניתוס is accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning; consistent with his known view
A person is a relative to himself, so he cannot testify about himself
A person cannot make himself wicked through his own testimony

steps.whatToRemember: A witness's admission of his own sin does not disqualify him, because his words about himself are not accepted. His words about the other person still count.
steps.confusionAlert: The borrower is not saying he did nothing wrong. The point is that בית דין does not use his own words to label him a רשע.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule in the laws of testimony: one statement can be accepted about another person and ignored about the speaker himself.

phrases.english: Rava follows his own reasoning,
for Rava said:
a person is a relative to himself,
and a person cannot make himself wicked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10 by citing another ruling of רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Citing the speaker's own principle: self-testimony is not accepted about oneself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The borrower admitted borrowing with interest, so he should be disqualified as a רשע.
steps.terutzMaskana: His admission about himself is ignored, so he stays a valid witness against בר ביניתוס.

steps.title: The butcher who sold טריפה meat
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן disqualified and removed a butcher who sold טריפה meat. After the butcher showed signs of regret, רב נחמן thought about reinstating him.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain butcher who was found to have let a טריפה go out from his hands. רב נחמן disqualified him and removed him. He went and let his hair and nails grow. רב נחמן thought to declare him fit again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story about a butcher caught selling non-kosher meat. It sets up the question of how such a person can be trusted again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling טריפה meat made the butcher a רשע, so he was disqualified as a witness and lost his job. Growing his hair and nails looked like a sign of real regret, so רב נחמן was ready to accept him back.

keyTerms.meaning: A butcher or slaughterer
A non-kosher animal with a fatal defect
He disqualified him (from testifying)
He removed him (from his job)
To declare him fit again

phrases.english: A certain butcher
about whom it was found that a tereifa went out
from under his hands,
phrases.notes: He means the butcher sold טריפה meat to people as if it were kosher.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman disqualified him and removed him.
He went and grew his hair and his nails.
phrases.notes: Letting his hair and nails grow was a way of showing he was sorry.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman thought to declare him fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case about disqualified people and how they can become valid again.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A butcher who sold טריפה is disqualified; רב נחמן considered reinstating him after outward signs of regret.

steps.title: Maybe he is only pretending
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects to רב נחמן: the butcher's regret may be fake, a trick to get his job back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Perhaps he is using a trick?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב נחמן's plan to reinstate the butcher. He points out that the signs of regret could be an act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The butcher has a strong reason to look sorry, since he wants his job and income back. Because of that, outward signs like growing hair and nails do not prove real תשובה.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, maybe
He is acting with trickery; faking it

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Perhaps he is acting with trickery?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's intention in step 12 to reinstate the butcher.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's plan to declare the butcher fit because of his signs of regret
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The butcher gains from looking sorry, so his outward behavior cannot prove real regret.

steps.title: So how can he fix his status?
steps.stepSummary: If outward regret is not enough, the גמרא asks what the butcher can do to be trusted again.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what is his remedy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question that sets up the next step. If signs of regret are not enough, what would prove he really changed?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's objection seems to leave the butcher with no way back. The גמרא asks for a test that would show real תשובה, one he couldn't fake for his own benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; but then
What
His remedy; his way to fix his status

phrases.english: Rather, what is his remedy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from רבא's objection: if fake regret is possible, what counts as real proof?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What action proves that someone suspected of selling טריפות has truly done תשובה?

steps.title: The test of real regret
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין rules that someone suspected of selling טריפות can be trusted again only after he gives up something valuable in a place where no one knows him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like רב אידי בר אבין, who said: One suspected of selling טריפות has no remedy until he goes to a place where they don't know him and returns a valuable lost item, or throws out his own valuable טריפה meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting רב אידי בר אבין. He gives a test that shows real regret.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a place where no one knows him, he gains nothing by acting honest, so he can't be doing it to get his job back. If he still loses real money to keep the law, by returning a lost item or throwing out his own טריפה, that proves his תשובה is real.

keyTerms.meaning: Suspected; someone who is not trusted
A remedy; a way to fix his status
A place where people don't know him
A lost item
Something of real value

steps.whatToRemember: Real תשובה is proven when a person gives up something valuable for the מצוה where he has nothing to gain from it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule for how a disqualified witness or butcher can become trusted again.

phrases.english: In accordance with Rav Idi bar Avin,
for Rav Idi bar Avin said:
One who is suspected regarding tereifot
has no remedy

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיֵּלֵךְ לְמָקוֹם שֶׁאֵין מַכִּירִין אוֹתוֹ
phrases.english: until he goes to a place where they do not know him
and returns a lost item of real value,
or he gets rid of a tereifa from under his hand
of real value, from his own property.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְרַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין, דְּאָמַר רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 with a ruling that avoids רבא's concern about faking.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He must give up something valuable for the מצוה, by returning a lost item or throwing out his own טריפה, in a place where no one knows him.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Outward signs of regret are not enough; only a costly act done where it brings no benefit proves real תשובה.

steps.title: What does 'those who fly pigeons' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase מפריחי יונים and asks what kind of person it is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה lists 'those who fly pigeons' as unfit witnesses. What does 'those who fly pigeons' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another group from the משנה's list of people who cannot be witnesses and asks what it means. This sets up the explanations that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Flying pigeons is not a sin in itself, so why would it make someone unfit to testify? The גמרא needs to know what kind of wrongdoing the משנה has in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who fly pigeons, listed in the משנה as unfit witnesses
What? (Aramaic)

phrases.english: And those who fly pigeons,
what is meant by 'those who fly pigeons'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the butcher discussion and returns to the משנה's list of unfit witnesses, taking up a new item.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What activity the משנה means by מפריחי יונים.

steps.title: First explanation: betting on pigeon races
steps.stepSummary: The scholars in בבל explain that it means people who bet on which pigeon will arrive first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here in בבל they explained it as someone who says: 'If your pigeon gets there before my pigeon, I will pay you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer is given: מפריחי יונים are people who gamble on pigeon races.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading, the problem is gambling. It is just like playing with dice, and that makes the person unfit to testify.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, meaning in בבל
They explained
If your pigeon gets ahead of my pigeon, the wording of a pigeon-race bet

phrases.english: Here they explained:
"If your pigeon gets ahead of my pigeon."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מפריחי יונים are people who bet on pigeon races.

steps.title: Second explanation: luring other people's pigeons
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא בר אושעיא explains that it means an ארא, someone who uses his pigeons to lure in pigeons from other people's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא בר אושעיא says: it means an ארא, a pigeon-luring trapper.
steps.whatsHappening: A second, different explanation is offered for מפריחי יונים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading, the problem is taking pigeons from around other people's property, which looks like a kind of stealing. Now there are two views, and the גמרא will ask why each one does not accept the other.

keyTerms.meaning: A trapper who trains his pigeons to bring in pigeons from other people's property

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama bar Oshaya said:
"A pigeon-luring trapper."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing answer to the same question that step 17 answered.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מפריחי יונים means an ארא, someone who lures in pigeons from other people's property.

steps.title: Why doesn't the first view accept the luring explanation?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the one who says 'pigeon racing' does not explain it as an ארא instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says it means 'if your pigeon gets ahead of my pigeon': why doesn't he say it means an ארא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins comparing the two views. First it asks the side that explains it as betting why it rejects the luring explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking other people's pigeons sounds like a good reason to disqualify a witness. So the גמרא wants to know what is wrong with that reading in the eyes of the first view.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says (this view)
What is the reason?

phrases.english: The one who says:
"If your pigeon gets ahead of my pigeon,"
what is the reason he does not say "a pigeon-luring trapper"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר אִי תִּקְדְּמֵיהּ יוֹנָךְ לְיוֹן מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר אָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two explanations by asking why the first view rejects the second.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the pigeon-racing view does not explain the משנה as an ארא.

steps.title: Luring is forbidden only for the sake of peace
steps.stepSummary: Taking pigeons that way is forbidden only because of דרכי שלום, so it is not real theft and would not disqualify a witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: an ארא is forbidden only because of the ways of peace.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first view's reason. Luring pigeons is not true stealing, so it is not serious enough to make someone unfit to testify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lured pigeons do not legally belong to anyone. The ban on taking them is only a rule to keep peace between neighbors. Breaking such a rule is not real גזל, so it does not make the person a פסול עדות.

keyTerms.meaning: He would say to you
The ways of peace: a rule made to prevent fights, not because something is truly stolen
Merely, only

phrases.english: He would say to you:
A pigeon-luring trapper is forbidden merely because of the ways of peace.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ אָרָא מִפְּנֵי דַּרְכֵי שָׁלוֹם בְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An ארא breaks only a peace-keeping rule, not a theft law, so he would not be disqualified.

steps.title: Why doesn't the second view accept the betting explanation?
steps.stepSummary: Now the גמרא asks why the one who says ארא does not explain it as pigeon-race betting.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who says it means an ארא: why doesn't he say it means 'if your pigeon gets ahead of my pigeon'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other side and asks why רבי חמא בר אושעיא rejects the betting explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gambling clearly disqualifies a witness. So the question is why the second view would not use that simple reading.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not say

phrases.english: And the one who says "a pigeon-luring trapper,"
what is the reason he does not say:
"If your pigeon gets ahead of my pigeon"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר אָרָא מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 19 by asking the opposite side for its reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the ארא view does not explain the משנה as pigeon-race betting.

steps.title: Pigeon betting is the same as dice playing
steps.stepSummary: Betting on pigeons is just another form of gambling, which the משנה already covers with משחק בקוביא, so מפריחי יונים must mean something new.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: that is the same as playing with dice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second view's reason. Pigeon-race betting is already included in the משנה's earlier item, the dice player.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already disqualifies משחק בקוביא, a gambler. Pigeon-race betting is the same kind of gambling, so listing it again would add nothing. That is why the second view says מפריחי יונים must mean something different: the ארא.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as
One who plays with dice, a gambler; already listed in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to read מפריחי יונים: betting on pigeon races, or luring other people's pigeons (ארא). The first view says luring is forbidden only because of דרכי שלום and is not real theft. The second view says pigeon betting is already covered by משחק בקוביא, and the first view answers that point in the next steps.

phrases.english: He would say to you:
That is the same as one who plays with dice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21. The other view responds to this argument in steps 23-24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Pigeon-race betting is already included in משחק בקוביא, so the משנה must mean the ארא.

steps.title: How does the other view answer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the view that explains מפריחי יונים as pigeon-race betting deals with the argument that this just repeats משחק בקוביא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other view, how does it answer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the view that says 'pigeon racing.' It asks how that view answers the argument from step 22. This one word sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 22, the view that says ארא argued that pigeon betting is just gambling, so it is already covered by משחק בקוביא. 'ואידך' asks the pigeon-racing view to explain why its reading is not a pointless repeat.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one: the other view in the dispute
Those who fly pigeons, the phrase in the משנה being explained

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: This is the one who says מפריחי יונים means betting on pigeon races. How does he answer the question from step 22?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the pigeon-racing view to answer the argument raised in step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the pigeon-racing reading is not already included in משחק בקוביא.

steps.title: Two different kinds of gambling
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches two kinds of gambling: dice, where the gambler depends on his own choice, and pigeons, where he depends on his pigeon.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה taught one who makes it depend on his own decision, and it taught one who makes it depend on his pigeon's decision.
steps.whatsHappening: The pigeon-racing view answers that the two cases in the משנה are different kinds of gambling, so neither one is extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With dice, the gambler thinks his own skill or choice decides the result. With pigeon racing, the result depends on the bird, which is outside his control. Because these two kinds of betting are different, the משנה lists them both.

keyTerms.meaning: He (the משנה) taught
Makes it depend on
On his own decision or judgment
On his pigeon's 'decision,' meaning how the bird performs
One who plays with dice, a gambler

phrases.english: It taught one who makes it depend on his own decision,
phrases.notes: This is the dice player, משחק בקוביא, who thinks he can control the outcome.

phrases.english: and it taught one who makes it depend on his pigeon's decision.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָא תּוֹלֶה בְּדַעַת עַצְמוֹ, וּתְנָא תּוֹלֶה בְּדַעַת יוֹנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23 by showing that the two cases in the משנה are different.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Dice betting depends on the gambler himself, and pigeon betting depends on the bird. These are two different kinds of gambling, so both are listed.

steps.title: Why both cases are needed: the dice case alone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a צריכא. If the משנה had taught only the dice case, we might think the gambler is a thief only there, because he never truly decides to hand over the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both are needed. If it had taught only the one who makes it depend on his own decision, I would say that only there he does not fully decide to transfer the money, because he says to himself:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to prove that the משנה needs both cases. It begins with what we would wrongly think if only the dice case were written. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dice player trusts his own skill, so he expects to win. When he bets, he never fully agrees to give up his money. That is why taking his money counts as stealing. The גמרא is about to quote what this gambler tells himself, and then it will explain why the pigeon case is still needed.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is needed: both cases have to be taught
There, in that case
Fully decides and transfers ownership

steps.confusionAlert: The דלא גמר ומקני part is about the loser of the bet. He never truly agreed to give up his money, so the winner who takes it is treated like a thief.

phrases.english: And it is necessary,
for if it had taught only one who makes it depend on his own decision,
it is there that he does not fully decide to transfer ownership,
as he says to himself:

steps.triggerLanguage: וּצְרִיכָא, דְּאִי תְּנָא תּוֹלֶה בְּדַעַת עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the answer of step 24 by starting to show why each of the two cases is needed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Partial so far. With dice alone, we might think the gambler is a thief only because he relies on himself and never truly agrees to give up the money.
